recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, pure ground-glass/non-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule 6mm or greater in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: a CT at 6-12 months to confirm persistence, and, only if the nodule is confirmed persistent, continued CT surveillance every 2 years until 5 years. The Local SOP's own wording states this boundary as '>6mm'; the governed executable boundary is '>=6mm', per explicit clinical HITL approval treating the Local SOP wording as an imprecise transcription of the underlying Fleischner 2017 source table (see clinical/sources/local-sop.json findings).

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends no routine follow-up for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule less than 6mm in whole-nodule diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. Per the primary Fleischner 2017 guideline, discrete solid components cannot be reliably defined in nodules this small, so no solid-component measurement is required or evaluated for this rule.

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule with whole-nodule diameter >=6mm and a solid component <6mm in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: a CT at 3-6 months to confirm persistence, and, only if the nodule is confirmed persistent, continued annual CT surveillance through 5 years. The Local SOP's own wording states only a simplified whole-nodule <6/>6mm trajectory with no solid-component distinction; the >=6mm boundary and the solid-component <6mm stratification are primary-Fleischner clarifications materially beyond the Local SOP text (see provenance anchors). A whole-nodule >=6mm nodule with a solid component >=6mm is a different, more suspicious Fleischner state and is explicitly out of scope for this rule.
